analysis:
Examined all supplied patches, BASE/HEAD source and mode metadata. ci-master.yml:80-89,102,143,230-239,249,290 disables cache restore/save on darkbloom-* runners lacking DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL. Its new pre-checkout checks (111-136,258-283) reject links, active hook files and selected executable/include config before the existing Git integrity checks. Cache keys, push-only saving, read-only permissions and persist-credentials:false remain unchanged. This is hardening, not a demonstrated security regression; the previously broader exposure to unsafe cached Git configuration is not reported as new.

Desktop frontend (desktop.yml:40-54) and Landing (landing.yml:38-51) apply equivalent gating to setup-node's npm cache without skipping installation or tests. Desktop's fixed-runner unsigned review package is unchanged. provider-release-cache.yml:84-93 exports the gate before calling provider-release-build at 103; master warming remains on Blacksmith and signing is not introduced.

Integration must verify that the changed composite build action consumes CI_ACTIONS_CACHE and that runner provisioning actually redirects Actions traffic when DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL is present: these workflows only test its presence, not configure the endpoint. Cache service authorization, branch/PR isolation and URL credential handling are outside this evidence. The Git validator's suppressed traversal/parser errors and special-file handling also warrant checking against the cache's actual writer trust contract, rather than assuming adversarial cache writes.

provider-tests.yml was supplied as metadata plus a truncated orientation patch; its complete changes cannot be assessed here. Review its gate propagation and repeated Git validation alongside the composite action. Build integrity is relevant to A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054, but no direct attestation, serving authorization, encryption, billing or runtime inference change is visible. T-041 concerns inference KV caching, not these CI caches, and its controls are untouched in this scope.
